# Saltwater Long Range Trip Planner

> Self-contained HTML dashboard for planning long-range saltwater fishing trips out of San Diego:
> aggregates trips from 11 long-range boats into a filterable Trip Finder, derives a Processing Planner of
> boat returns per day (long-range + multi-day boats from the four SD landings), and adds a Processing Calculator comparing two San Diego fish processors.
> Pure HTML/CSS/JS in one file — no server, no build step.

## Start here
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): canonical agent guide — GitHub operations rules, Contents API protocol, scraping workarounds.
- [README.md](README.md): human quickstart — features, usage, data sources, refresh instructions.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): version history, newest first.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): commit + README standard.

## Dashboard
- [index.html](index.html): GitHub Pages entry point — redirects to the dashboard file below.
- [saltwater_trip_planner.html](saltwater_trip_planner.html): the entire dashboard — Trip Finder, Processing Planner, and Processing Calculator tabs; long-range trip data lives in the inline `RAW` JS array (return dates derived from departure + trip length); multi-day rows live in the auto-generated `MULTI` block (return date/time as posted). Tests: `node test-multiday.js`, `python3 tests/test_refresh_multiday.py`.

## Refresh
- [refresh_multiday.py](refresh_multiday.py): headless multi-day refresh (four landings) — writes data/ and the MULTI-DAY block; tests in tests/.

## Key rules
- Single self-contained HTML file: all CSS/JS inline, opens via file://, no external dependencies, no localStorage (in-memory state only).
- Trip data is a snapshot — every refresh must update the visible "data as of" disclaimer and README data-freshness note, and link to live sources.
- fishingreservations.net blocks rapid automated requests (CAPTCHA error 338): refresh data by reading pre-loaded browser tabs, never rapid sequential scraping.
- Long-range rows: return dates are derived from departure + trip length. Multi-day rows (MULTI block, auto-generated): return date/time are stored as posted by the landing, never hand-edited.
- GitHub updates go through the Contents API: GET the file sha first, then PUT with sha; skipping the GET causes a 409.
- Data refresh commits use the `data` type with a body of at least 3 bullets; README updated on every feat/fix/data commit.
